title: senior-team-tuning-prep-and-decision-backlog
content:
Purpose: quick prep for the senior leadership sync (weekly exec-staff) — align on three prioritized asks, clarify fallback paths, and surface one cross-org risk for decision.

Meeting context: Clara is running this one solo; several items are still half-baked. This doc is a scratchpad to pull into the 1:1 with Ethan and the broader staff meeting. Keep comments inline and highlight anything that should be a hard stop in the deck.

Meeting logistics
- Time: 2026-03-15 09:00 PT (30m)
- Attendees: CEO, CTO, Head of Product, Head of Eng (Ethan), Head of Ops (Maya), Clara (host), Ravi (SRE observer)
- Goal: get agreed next steps for (A) Dedicated capacity rollout gating, (B) Hosted API latency mitigation, (C) Private deploy pricing guardrails.

Topline snapshot (one-liners to read aloud)
- Dedicated: pilot customers (3) onboarded; observed 18% higher P95 than target under mixed workloads; root cause likely autoscaler mis-tuning + cold-starts.
- Hosted API: tail latency regressions after backend kernel patch 289 — rollback possible but loses throughput gains.
- Private: legal asked for a hard cap option in the quote; Sales needs a simple guardrail to avoid margin erosion.

Priority asks for the meeting (ranked)
1) Approve a canary rollback window for kernel patch PR#289 (hosted) OR sign-off for a gradual rollback with throughput monitoring. Decision needed: rollback fully now vs staged revert.
   - Risk if we rollback: lose ~12% throughput at median; benefit: remove 200–400ms P95 spikes in some regions.
   - If we delay: continue supporting customers but risk SLA breaches and noise.
2) For Dedicated rollout: greenlight a sprint of autoscaler parameter resets + targeted pre-warm for top 2 pilot customers; commit $Xk spend for bespoke pre-warm nodes for two weeks. Decision: approve spend and escalation path.
3) Private pricing guardrail: set a default max-discount rule in quotes to protect margin until we have real usage curves (ask is to approve temporary pricing cap policy).

Background + evidence (short)
- Telemetry: INF-4123 shows 45 incidents over last 10 days tied to long-tail kernel stalls; stack traces point to new kernel selection heuristic introduced in PR 289.
- Customer notes: Pilot A reported two degraded windows during peak which maps to pre-warm eviction events.
- Finance: model shows Dedicated pilot at current discounts would drop blended margin below 18% at 3-month run-rate (spreadsheet linked in Confluence).

Suggested framing / language for the meeting
- Lead with customer impact (pilot reliability), then trade-offs (latency vs throughput), then ask (specific decision and fallback).
- Use hard absolutes only where necessary: e.g., "approve a 2-week staged rollback starting 3/16 if P95 > 600ms in EU region".

Open questions (need input before finalizing slides)
- Ethan: how fast can autoscaler param change be pushed to Dedicated pools without disruption?
- Maya: do we have an exact cost estimate for 2-week pre-warm nodes (including egress/ops)?
- Ravi/SRE: is there a safe staged rollback plan for PR#289 that preserves latest kernel path for low-latency requests?

Metrics mini-table (paste into slide if needed)
- Median latency (hosted): 42ms -> post-PR 37ms (good)
- P95 latency (hosted): 540ms -> post-PR 720ms (bad)
- Dedicated throughput: target 10k rps -> observed 9.2k rps under mixed seq lengths
- Pilot margin estimate (month 1): 22% -> with current discounts ~16%

Proposed slide flow (3 slides only)
1) TL;DR + ask (single slide)
2) Evidence + trade-offs (graphs: P95 trend, throughput histogram)
3) Decision table + immediate next actions (who owns what in next 48hrs)

Immediate next actions (48–72h) — include in meeting close
- If rollback approved: Engineering to cut a staged rollback branch (owner: Ethan) and SRE to prepare traffic-splits (owner: Ravi). ETA: 48h.
- If rollback rejected: Ops to open emergency runbook and schedule a midnight mitigation window to apply temporary patch (owner: Maya). ETA: 36h.
- Dedicated pre-warm: Finance to confirm $ figure and sign-off (owner: Finance PM — placeholder: Priya). ETA: 24h.
- Pricing cap: Product ops to draft a temporary policy and legal to greenlight language (owners: Maya + Legal). ETA: 72h.

Action tracker (for me — Clara)
- Prepare 1-slide TL;DR + speaker notes (due 2026-03-13) — DONE (draft attached).
- Sync with Ethan 1:1 to confirm rollback technical plan (booked 2026-03-13 11:00) — TODO.
- Pull exact cost numbers from Priya and inject into slide (due 2026-03-14) — TODO.
- Call out specific customers to PMs for outreach (A, B, C) and draft templated note (due 2026-03-14) — TODO.

Playbook snippets (notes-to-self)
- If kernel rollback: keep throughput test harness running in parallel to compare median/throughput delta live.
- If pre-warm spend approved: ensure tagging and chargeback so Finance can attribute pilot delta to the program.
- Keep messaging tight: "temporary mitigation while we validate kernel heuristics" — avoid overpromising long-term revert.

Potential friction points to surface during meeting
- Sales will push back on pricing cap (short-term quota pressure). Suggest offering a "pilot exception" window with guardrails.
- Eng may resist rollback because it erases recent perf wins; emphasize risk of SLA churn vs incremental throughput.

Notes for 1:1 with Ethan (prep items)
- Ask for a short, 2-minute technical brief: cause hypothesis, rollback steps, estimated regression on median throughput, monitoring hooks.
- Confirm rollback automation: can we do a canary in 10% of traffic with kill-switch? Who owns the kill-switch?
- Confirm risk matrix: what other subsystems might regress if kernel path changes? (KV cache, batching scheduler)

Unresolved / parking lot
- Long-term plan for kernel auto-selection — needs a cross-team RFC (not for this meeting).
- Deeper cost model for private deployments (product ops to own).

Bottom line (one sentence to say out loud)
- We need a time-boxed decision: either stage a rollback starting next week with clear monitoring and rollback kill-switch, or accept short-term risk and fund immediate mitigations for pilot customers; recommend staged rollback + pre-warm spend.

Quick links (for slide/handout)
- Confluence: INF-serve-runtime-rollout-2026 (linked)
- Jira: INF-4123 (incident list)
- PR: runtime PR#289 (perf kernel changes)

Last-minute checklist before the run (Clara)
- [ ] Finalize TL;DR slide and open with customer anecdote
- [ ] Add exact cost numbers and legal blurb for pricing cap
- [ ] Confirm Ethan 1:1 and insert his 2-line technical summary into slide notes
- [ ] Print (PDF) or add to shared drive for execs before start

End of scratchpad.

(Comments encouraged — collab: Ethan/Maya/Ravi. If anyone wants to delete sections or flag stronger language, mark with initials and date.)
